about.title: About
about.bio: I'm Carlos, a software engineer based in Mérida, Mexico. I build web platforms, desktop tools and AI features, from a commercial suite of Revit add-ins for construction teams to an investment tracker with a multi-model AI analyst. I studied physics and mathematics, and it shows in the work I enjoy most: geometry, financial math and models that have to be right. I build with coding agents like Claude Code as part of my daily workflow, and I work remotely with teams anywhere.

fibrantAnalyst.title: The AI analyst's tool use
fibrantAnalyst.description: A question goes to the model you choose: Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, with usage metered in credits by tier. The model runs on a static, cache-friendly system prompt and the portfolio's own memory, and reads the portfolio through tool use, from Supabase behind row-level security, before it answers.

vdcSystem.title: VDC Plugins: add-in, licensing and subscriptions
vdcSystem.description: The storefront offers a free trial and the installer download. Every Revit add-in checks the user's subscription before it runs, and Stripe manages organisation and personal subscriptions.

f1Pipeline.title: The F1 Forecast Lab pipeline
f1Pipeline.description: Race data comes in through FastF1 and passes leakage checks. Logistic regression, LightGBM and XGBoost models, with calibration, are compared on event- and season-level backtests. The f1-weekend operator CLI and a Supabase sync feed a Next.js dashboard of predicted against actual results.

expressusCheckout.title: Expressus Café checkout
expressusCheckout.description: A guest's cart lives on an HTTP-only cookie. Skydropx quotes the shipping, a transactional database function calculates the checkout totals, and the customer pays through Stripe Checkout. A signed webhook then leads to the stock change, also in a transactional database function.

forgeClashFlow.title: Forge Clash Insight flow
forgeClashFlow.description: The user signs in with Autodesk (APS/ACC) or Procore. Models from different disciplines are processed and aligned, and several collision-detection algorithms find the clashes. Each clash gets a 0–10 score, weighted by a priority matrix of building systems. The results go to a Three.js viewer and to an LLM that summarises each area of the building.
